title: Isolation, and what actually contains code
summary: One question asked at four depths: when this code does the worst thing it can, what stops it? A process stops almost nothing, a container is namespaces and cgroups over a kernel everything still shares, and a virtual machine buys a second kernel at a price that decided what the people running other people's code actually built. Hone is its own worked example here, because the grader runs submitted code and node:vm is documented in this repo as a convenience rather than a boundary. The last page is the case a web engineer now meets weekly, which is running code a model wrote. Packaging and deploying an image belong to production; this section owns isolation as a security property.
